evidence.title: File:Higos con queso.jpg
evidence.description: Fig candy is a traditional Ecuadorian dessert made up of the fruit of the fig tree and fresh cheese or cheese. This dessert is cooked for about three days, caramelizing the figs in piloncillo (panela honey) the third of them and adding the desired spices, cinnamon, for example. It is typical that figs with cheese are served as a dessert for fanesca, the star dish of Easter in the Andean country.

A whole New York-style cheesecake with a golden-brown baked top, presented on a decorative glass plate. The cake is garnished with fresh whole strawberries arranged around the base, their green leaves pointing outward. 
 The cheesecake sits on a red tablecloth with a holiday-themed pattern featuring snowflakes and branches. In the background, part of a chocolate cake with green frosting decoration is visible, along with white plates, a glass of water, and other table settings, suggesting a festive or celebratory dessert table. 
 
The photograph is taken from a slight angle, focusing on the cheesecake.
